# Dusk

> Dusk is a free, open-source (MIT) macOS menu-bar app: a blue light filter (6500K down to 500K), screen dimmer below minimum brightness, PWM flicker-free mode for MacBook built-in displays, and a switch to disable temporal dithering on Apple silicon. Free alternative to f.lux, Night Shift, Sundown and Iris. No account, no telemetry, no network.

- Repository: https://github.com/s-azizkhan/dusk-mac
- Download: https://github.com/s-azizkhan/dusk-mac/releases/latest
- Website: https://s-azizkhan.github.io/dusk-mac/
- Platform: macOS 14 Sonoma or later, Apple silicon and Intel (universal)
- License: MIT
- Install (Homebrew): `brew install --cask s-azizkhan/tap/dusk`
- Install (manual): download Dusk-macOS.zip, move Dusk.app to Applications, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Dusk.app`, open it.

## Features
- Colour temperature 500K-6500K, 7 presets (Energy 6000K, Daylight 5000K, Evening 3400K, Night 2700K, Late 1900K, Deep 1200K, Midnight 500K)
- Software dimming to 5%
- Flicker-free: backlight held at 100% via DisplayServices, dimming done in the gamma table
- Disable temporal dithering: IORegistry `enableDither = false` on IOMobileFramebufferAP
- Night schedule, launch at login

## Docs
- [README](https://github.com/s-azizkhan/dusk-mac/blob/main/README.md): features, FAQ, comparison with Night Shift, f.lux and Sundown
